newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PRIVATE XIOSBANK ENTERS BANKASSURANCE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PRIVATE XIOSBANK ENTERS BANKASSURANCE.

text.p: Greek private Xiosbank, which has applied for listing on the Athens bourse, is entering bankassurance with two new insurance investment products, its chairman Yannis Pehlivanides told a news conference.

"Xiosbank makes a dynamic entry into the bankassurance field from today," said Pehlivanidis. "The bank ...created two new friendly insurance-investment products: a pension plan and a plan for children coming of age."
They are basically two investment products with an insurance wrap up which are designed to pass all cost saving benefits to investors unlike plans offered by insurance firms, he said.

Investors will pay a monthly premium that will be invested in Xiosbank's fixed income fund, ranked first in its fund class with a return of 16.8 percent return in 1996, and will receive a lump sum after a pre-agreed time period.
Tassos Pagonis, the director of insurance products at Xiosbank, said he would be satisfied if the 1997 total annual premiums from selling these products to investors exceeded 800 million drachmas.
Lloyds London will provide the necessary insurance coverage, said Pagonis.
Xiosbank saw its pre-tax profits rise 20 percent to 2.1 billion drachmas in 1996 base on preliminary data, said Pehlivanidis.
Lending posted an increase of 24 percent to 103 billion drachmas in 1996 with consumer loans accounting for 67 billion drachmas and business loans for 36 billion.

According to Bank of Greece figures, the Xiosbank enjoyed a market share of 9.0 percent in consumer loans and 8.0 percent in auto loans as of June 1996, said its chairman. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
